relevance_note: Case report of an HA20 proband with a TNFAIP3 variant and her affected family: "we present the first patient with HA20, who was previously diagnosed with AOSD but later found to have a novel heterozygous variant in TNFAIP3".
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; values were typed into a Python builder that copies each span from the paper text (thin spaces U+2009 kept as printed) and the result was checked for verbatim spans and complete fields. No tables with patients exist; the only supplementary file (Table S1) is a gnomAD/MRF residue table without patient data. Scope: 4 people — the proband ('patient'; the paper calls her 'the patient', 'the proband' and 'the index case'), her two children and her father. The paper writes 'two children, a boy aged 6 and a half and a girl of age 4 years', so the children are labelled 'daughter of patient' and 'son of patient' (the words daughter/son are not printed); the father is 'the father of the index case'. Children's variant rows are based on 'The proband’s two children ... were also investigated for autosomal dominant inheritance' and 'Genetic analysis of family members found segregation with the inflammatory clinical phenotypes (Figure 1A)': the paper does not say in words which family members were genotyped or that each child carries the variant, so these rows rest on the segregation statement; zygosity and inheritance for the children are left 'not reported' (not stated, rule 8). The father (early onset RA) has no variant row: the paper does not say he was tested. The proband's inheritance is not reported. Variant: the authors first called c.1906C>T missense, then describe it as an exonic splice variant at the last residue of exon 7 causing deletion of exon 8 in cDNA and p.His636fsTer1; variant_type recorded as 'splice' following the title and Figure 1 legend. The codon notation printed is 'n.1972 Cgt/Tgt' and 'c.1906 Cat/TAG'; not reconciled. The proband's age_at_diagnosis (21) is the age at the clinical AOSD diagnosis; the age at genetic HA20 diagnosis is not given. The daughter's disease label 'HA20' rests on the Discussion's 'the younger sibling we presented here' among HA20 cases (the girl, 4 years, is younger than the boy, 6.5 years, and responded to colchicine); the son has no explicit diagnosis label. The Discussion's 'clinical presentation varying from periodic fever-like illness, AOSD to RA' within the family was not mapped to individuals. Vital status 'alive' is taken from present-tense statements about current care. Checklist: the proband's negative ANA, RF and ACPA are recorded as excluded features but 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' is left 'not reported' under the narrow-vs-broad rule (other autoantibodies are not addressed). Negative blood and urine cultures were not used to exclude 'recurrent infections'. The daughter's 'pain in her knees' was taken as arthralgia (observed). The father's 'early onset RA' was taken as arthritis (observed). n_patients_reported is null because the authors do not state a count of variant carriers; cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null because the paper says nothing about earlier publication of these patients. No contradictions about a person's features were found.

functional_evidence_statement.value: proband cDNA showed a mutant allele with deletion of exon 8; loss of transcript by nonsense-mediated decay with A20 haploinsufficiency confirmed by Western blot; greater percentage of p65-positive monocytes after LPS than healthy controls (not statistically significant); significantly increased IL-1β and IL-18 (NLRP3-dependent) and other cytokines from PBMC after LPS+ATP; significantly higher serum ASC specks than healthy control range
span: The patient’s cDNA produced a mutant allele containing deletion of exon 8 (Figure 1B).
Loss of transcript by nonsense-mediated decay resulting in A20 haploinsufficiency was confirmed by Western blot (Figure 1C).
Following stimulation, greater percentage of patient monocytes became p65 positive compared with monocytes from healthy controls. However, this did not reach a statistical significance (Figure 2).

The production of IL-1β and IL-18 was found to be significantly increased in the patient’s PBMC compared with healthy controls after stimulation by priming and activation with LPS and ATP, respectively (Figures 3A,B).
We found that patient serum contained significantly higher numbers of ASC specks compared with our healthy control range (Figure 3I).
